clue.text: Class for which average pug or boxer may qualify

definitions.text: Class for which average pug or boxer may qualify

parts.words: Class for which average pug or boxer may qualify
parts.note: read 'average' as the middle of the scale and 'pug' as a prizefighter: the clue describes a boxing division named after a mid-range body mass

explanation.surface: A remark on which category an ordinary fighter or his dog might enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pug' and 'boxer' both look like dog breeds, but here each means a prizefighter; 'average' points to the middle of the boxing divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing is split into classes by body mass, and the one between welter and light-heavy is named for its mid position.

clue.text: Doctor is not involved in proposals

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a standard abbreviation for a doctor

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of 'is not' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A medic stays out of the suggestions being put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the abbreviation MO; 'involved' jumbles IS NOT into TIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal suggestions put to a meeting for a vote are called motions, the same as proposals.

clue.text: Write up note in journal of food allowance

indicators.note: in places the turned note inside the word for journal

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing upward means the word for note is read bottom to top

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone records a musical note in their journal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Write up' means read upwards, so the note gives ET; 'in' sets it within the journal word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a regulated daily ration of food, as in a hospital or prison, is an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Novelist composed backchat — in old Mauretania?

indicators.note: in puts the turned chat inside the ship word

parts.note: the Mauretania was a famous Cunard ocean liner of the early twentieth century
read as chat backwards: chat is TALK, turned round to KLAT

explanation.surface: A writer produces cheeky retorts while aboard an old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backchat' is read as 'chat back', giving KLAT; 'in' sets it within the ship. Eric Linklater was a Scottish novelist; 'composed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Linklater was a twentieth-century Scottish writer of fiction such as Juan in America.

clue.text: Rate set on a northern town.

parts.note: to rate is to scold severely, as is to ... old verb for a dressing-down

explanation.surface: A local tax is imposed on a town in the North of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like a tax but is the old verb meaning to scold. Wigan is a town in Lancashire in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wigan is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.

clue.text: Opportunity to score over opponents

parts.note: a cricket turn at the crease, when a side gets its chance to pile up runs, also a general word for a spell of opportunity

explanation.surface: A chance to get the better of rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' hints at cricket, where a side's batting turn is its chance to put runs on the board; cricket is a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a side's batting turn is the period in which it can make runs, and figuratively any spell of chance.

clue.text: Tisane WPC might take to her beat, maybe

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters of 'her beat' may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A policewoman might carry a calming drink with her on patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: A WPC was a woman police constable in Britain; her beat is her patrol route. 'maybe' rearranges HER BEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an infusion of dried leaves or flowers rather than true tea.

clue.text: They offer inclusive terms for taking parcel to French town

parts.note: a package is a parcel
Tours is a city on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: Holiday deals take a parcel to a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidays sold with travel, hotel and meals bundled together at one price are all-in deals.

clue.text: The sight of a bathing beauty turned him into a beast

definitions.text: The sight of a bathing beauty turned him into a beast

parts.words: The sight of a bathing beauty turned him into a beast
parts.note: the Greek myth of the hunter who saw the goddess Artemis bathing and was changed into a stag, then torn apart by his own hounds

explanation.surface: A man so smitten by a swimmer that he behaved like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned him into a beast' sounds like lust, but it is literal: Artemis (Diana) changed the hunter into a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the hunter who spied the goddess Artemis bathing was transformed into a deer as punishment.

clue.text: Princess may travel by new liner

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of 'liner' are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A royal might take a trip on a freshly launched ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liner' looks like a ship to travel on, but 'new' makes it anagram fodder, giving NERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril is the eldest daughter of King Lear in Shakespeare's play, so a royal daughter.

clue.text: Do they reveal the false position the golfer is in?

definitions.text: Do they reveal the false position the golfer is in?

parts.words: Do they reveal the false position the golfer is in?
parts.note: a golfer's ball position is called its lie, and a lie is also a falsehood; devices that expose untruths are described as if they found a golf ball

explanation.surface: A question about gadgets that show where a golfer's ball has landed badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf ball's position is its 'lie', so 'false position' plays on lie as an untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygraphs are machines meant to show when a person is telling untruths.

clue.text: King, rejecting Hadrian's work, claims to have the answers

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
rejecting is saying no
Hadrian's Wall was built by the Roman emperor Hadrian across northern England

explanation.surface: A monarch dismisses the Roman emperor's frontier and acts as though he is omniscient.
explanation.walkthrough: Hadrian's Wall is the Roman barrier across northern England. The definition describes the person by what they do.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is someone who behaves as if they are an expert on everything.

clue.text: Double negative by this girl on the stage

definitions.text: Double negative by this girl on the stage

parts.words: Double negative by this girl on the stage
parts.note: a 1920s musical's title puts two refusals in front of a girl's name, so the doubled negative stands beside her on stage

explanation.surface: A grammatical slip made by an actress in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical 'No, No, Nanette' opens with a double negative before the heroine's name.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the title heroine of the 1925 musical comedy whose name follows two refusals.

clue.text: Mannering, extremely sweet in himself, is liable to bluster

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the hero's first name

parts.note: Guy Mannering is the title hero of a Walter Scott novel

indicators.note: extremely takes only the extremes of the word sweet, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A character named Mannering, very sweet at heart, tends to rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'himself' points back to Mannering, Scott's hero, whose first name takes the sweet word's first and last letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather blows in sudden blasts, as blustery wind does.

clue.text: Check speed of climb as measure of duration

parts.note: to time something is to check how fast it goes with a clock
to scale is to climb

explanation.surface: A climber's rate of ascent is used to measure how long something takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A timescale is the period over which events happen or are planned, a span of time.

clue.text: It has to do with changing one's make-up, naturally

definitions.text: It has to do with changing one's make-up, naturally

parts.words: It has to do with changing one's make-up, naturally
parts.note: make-up here is the body's chemistry, and the natural processes that turn food into tissue and energy are being described

explanation.surface: Something concerned with altering cosmetics in a natural way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics but means the body's constitution, changed by chemical processes.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to the chemical processes by which the body converts food into energy and tissue.

clue.text: The last shall be first in island following leading saint in utmost confidence

indicators.note: following means the turned island comes after the top saint

parts.note: top means leading

indicators.note: the biblical saying signals moving the final letter of the island to the front

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A biblical promise of reversal on an island, after a prominent saint, told in strict confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical 'The last shall be first' moves the island's final letter to its front, giving ECRET; 'following' puts that after the top saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Information marked top secret is meant to be shared only with a trusted few, the highest level of confidentiality.

clue.text: This is the form — get it?

definitions.meaning: a likeness, the shape or image of something
do you get the ...? means do you understand

explanation.definitionFit: A painting or image shows a shape, and to see the whole scene is to understand.

clue.text: Sty is a blot on the landscape

definitions.meaning: a sty is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye
an ugly building or sight that spoils a view

explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an ailment of the eyelid, and an ugly feature spoiling a view is called the same thing.

clue.text: Throw-back to lioness born in Switzerland

indicators.note: a throw-back sends the lioness's name back the other way

parts.note: Elsa is the lioness of Joy Adamson's book Born Free

explanation.surface: A reminder of a famous lioness born in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsa was the lioness raised by Joy Adamson in 'Born Free'; 'Throw-back to' turns her name into ASLE, after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Basle, or Basel, is a city on the Rhine in northern Switzerland.

clue.text: Improper EEC line gets the bird

parts.note: blue means risqué or improper
CAP, the Common Agricultural Policy, was the EEC's farming policy line

explanation.surface: An indecent European policy gets jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being booed, but the bird is the definition: a bluecap is a blue tit. The EEC was the forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluecap is a regional name for the blue tit, a small European songbird.

clue.text: It may be stewed, fried or soused

definitions.text: It may be stewed, fried or soused

parts.words: It may be stewed, fried or soused
parts.note: the three cooking words are all slang for drunk, so the clue describes a tipsy state rather than food

explanation.surface: A dish that can be cooked in any of three ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed', 'fried' and 'soused' look like cooking methods but are all slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk, as are the three words in the clue.

clue.text: Pawnee accepts article however dirty

indicators.note: accepts here means the pawnbroker takes on the article after him

parts.note: the pawnee is the one who takes a pledge, i.e. the pawnbroker, known in old slang as uncle
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Native American takes in an object, however filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawnee' looks like the Native American people but means the person a pledge is pawned with; 'uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means soiled or impure, a direct synonym for filthy.

clue.text: Following Virginia she gets a butterfly

indicators.note: Following means the girl's name comes after the state abbreviation, so taking that away leaves her

parts.note: Vanessa is the genus of butterflies including the red admiral
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A woman named after Virginia catches a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: VA followed by the girl's name makes VANESSA, a butterfly genus, so the name is VANESSA without VA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessa is a girl's name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Praise for a nose

definitions.meaning: a compliment or bunch of flowers given in praise
a wine's nose is its aroma

explanation.definitionFit: A tribute of flowers or compliments, and also the scent of a wine as judged by tasters.

clue.text: Senseless conditions set for Proust's characters

indicators.note: set means arranged, so those letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters making up the word Proust's, with its S

explanation.surface: A novelist's people are described as being in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people in a novel but means letters: the letters of PROUST'S, set anew.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness, so plural dazed states without feeling.

clue.text: A match for the devil

definitions.meaning: an old name for a friction match

explanation.definitionFit: Lucifers were early friction matches, and the name is also given to Satan.

clue.text: Topping fee at the end of a contract job?

definitions.text: Topping fee at the end of a contract job?

parts.words: Topping fee at the end of a contract job?
parts.note: topping is slang for killing, so a hired killer's fee for a contract is described like a payment on being dismissed

explanation.surface: A bonus fee paid when a hitman finishes a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' and 'contract' suggest murder for hire; the real sense is the lump sum paid when employment is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to an employee whose job ends, compensation for being let go.
